paper.title_en: Dynamic analysis of an LDM quantum Cournot duopoly game with product substitutability
paper.abstract_en: This paper constructs a quantum Cournot duopoly model for two-product competition by merging principles from quantum game theory and nonlinear dynamics. By introducing squeezing parameters $\alpha $ and $\beta $, the Li-Du-Massar (LDM) quantization scheme is extended to a four-dimensional system, which is used to characterize the coordination of product strategies. Under the assumption of bounded rationality of firms, the model adopts a discrete-time dynamic system for output adjustment and analyzes the stability of equilibrium via Jacobian eigenvalues and the Jury criterion. Numerical simulations demonstrate the complex dynamic behaviors of the system, including bifurcation, high-dimensional singular attractors and stability regions. Entanglement and adjustment speed exert a crucial influence on maintaining the stability of the quantum equilibrium: The equilibrium remains stable under conditions of low adjustment speed or low entanglement, whereas high adjustment speed or high entanglement triggers bifurcation and chaos. Increased entanglement compresses the stable region and raises market uncertainty. Finally, this paper conducts a comparative analysis with Yang and Gong's bounded-rational continuous-variable quantum game model.
